parties: Share India Securities Limited (transferee); Silverleaf Capital Services Private Limited (transferor)
headline: NCLT Ahmedabad approves Scheme of Amalgamation of Silverleaf Capital Services into Share India Securities
sum: NCLT Ahmedabad Bench-I has approved the Scheme of Amalgamation of Silverleaf Capital Services Private Limited with Share India Securities Limited, effective by regulatory order dated 20 August 2026, completing a financial services consolidation in the securities broking ecosystem.
implication: NCLT Scheme approval is the final gate for statutory amalgamation; post-order, the transferee assumes all assets, liabilities and statutory obligations of the transferor without separate novation of material contracts, but operational integration and regulatory re-licensing (NSE/BSE membership, SEBI stock broker registration) remain mandatory before full functional merger.
detail: Share India Securities Limited, a listed equity broker, has obtained final approval from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Ahmedabad Bench-I, for the amalgamation of its subsidiary or affiliate Silverleaf Capital Services Private Limited. The order dated 20 August 2026 marks the completion of the scheme approval phase under the Companies Act, 2013; the amalgamation scheme would have been filed at NCLT following board approvals and shareholder consent (for the transferee company). This is a vertical or horizontal consolidation within the financial services sector, likely designed to streamline duplicate regulatory registrations, consolidate client books, or absorb operational capabilities. Post-NCLT approval, Share India Securities must file certified copies with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) Delhi; the scheme becomes effective on RoC registration, triggering automatic transfer of all assets and liabilities.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Sections 230–232 (Scheme of Amalgamation and Merger)
framework.note: central; defines the filing, approval process at NCLT, shareholder/creditor rights, and statutory effect of the scheme order.

framework.ref: Companies (Court) Rules, 2016, Rules 1–17 (NCLT Procedure for Schemes)
framework.note: central; governs NCLT petition filing, convening meeting direction, shareholder voting threshold (75%), creditor objections, and the order-issuing timeline.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Stock Brokers and Sub-brokers) Regulations, 2020
framework.note: amended; the transferee must ensure compliance with registration, net worth, auditor appointment, and know-your-client norms post-amalgamation; SEBI may require updated registration or certificate.

framework.ref: NSE/BSE Listing Agreements and Membership Rules
framework.note: central; if Silverleaf holds direct NSE or BSE membership or clearing member status, the transferee must assume or separately apply for membership; failure risks client settlement disruption.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961, Section 47 (Amalgamation - Tax-Neutral Transfer)
framework.note: if the scheme qualifies as a statutory amalgamation, no capital gains tax on asset transfer; ensure conditions (100% shareholding or scheme condition) met for the exemption.
if Silverleaf holds beneficiary owner accounts or depository participant credentials, those must be merged or transferred; depository instructions required.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, Section 230A (Pre-Pack Merger)
framework.note: only if either party is under insolvency; otherwise inapplicable. If triggered, the process is expedited, but no indication in this filing.

conditions: Filing of certified NCLT order with Registrar of Companies, Delhi (activates statutory amalgamation)
NSE and/or BSE approval/notification of membership transfer or transferee's separate membership application (if applicable)
SEBI re-registration or certificate renewal for the transferee post-merger
Depository (NSDL/CDSL) notification of beneficiary account and DP credential mergers (if applicable)
approvals: Transferee (Share India Securities) shareholder approval (presumed pre-filing)
Registrar of Companies, Delhi (pending certificate issue post-filing)
structure.novel: None evident from filing; this is a standard two-company amalgamation within the regulated broking sector under Companies Act s.230–232.

triggers.note: Mandatory NCLT approval for amalgamation; no scheme becomes effective until RoC registration.

triggers.law: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Stock Brokers and Sub-brokers) Regulations, 2020
triggers.note: Transferee must maintain SEBI registration, net worth, auditor, and grievance redressal post-merger or apply for amended registration.

triggers.law: NSE/BSE Listing Rules or Membership Rules
triggers.note: If Silverleaf holds direct membership, transferee must assume it or separately apply; membership continuity is critical for settlement and clearing.
